params.prompt:
1950s theatrical cartoon slapstick, hand-drawn colored-pencil pencil-test animation on cream paper, held on twos with visible line boil. Fixed camera, locked tripod, one continuous shot.

The small terracotta cube creature sitting on the floor lowers its pencil, draws in a huge breath that lifts it up tall and stiff with its shoulders hunched up to its ears, holds it for a beat, and lets it all out in one big happy whoosh — its whole body drops soft and loose, its shoulders fall, its eyes squeeze shut and its smile spreads wide. It wipes the back of one hand across its brow in one quick sweep and flicks it away. It gives one small happy hop on the spot, lands, and settles back into its seat beaming, eyes open, smile wide.

Its face is two small dark dot eyes, two short brows and a small happy smile — the same happy face in every frame. It holds exactly one pencil in every frame. It stays sitting in the same spot on the floor in every frame. It stays small, tinier than the bookshelf's lower shelf, in every frame. The three towers of paper stand in the same places and reach out of the top of the frame in every frame; the loose sheets on the floor lie still where they are in every frame; the small desk, the bookshelf of binders and the grey filing cabinet stay the same drawings in every frame.

Squash and stretch on every accent, smear frames through the fast arcs, snappy timing, elastic overshoot, comic energy.
